title: Tortilla Española
subtitle: Spanish omelette with potatoes and onion
excerpt: The iconic Spanish egg and potato omelette: sliced potatoes and onion cooked very gently in olive oil until completely soft, then mixed with beaten eggs and cooked slowly into a thick, just-set disc that is flipped to cook on both sides. Eaten warm or at room temperature.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tortilla española (Spanish omelette, not to be confused with the Mexican corn tortilla) is one of the defining dishes of Spanish cuisine, eaten for breakfast, lunch, and dinner, as a tapa, bocadillo filling, or main course. There is a long-running debate about whether the onion is traditional or not (the tortilla without onion is tortilla sin cebolla); the version with onion is more widely made and the more common in restaurants and bars. The key technique is the slow confit of the potato and onion in olive oil, which produces a very different result from simply boiling or frying: the potato becomes creamy and sweet and soaks up the oil. The flip is the moment of anxiety: a plate or lid is placed over the pan and the omelette is inverted in one confident movement. The centre should remain creamy and slightly underdone (cuajada is the term for just-set).

recipeTools.notes: A 24 to 26 cm non-stick frying pan.

content.text: Confiting the potato and onion in olive oil is not the same as frying them: use very low heat and take 20 to 25 minutes. The potato should be completely soft and just beginning to collapse. Mix the egg and potato thoroughly and leave to rest for 10 minutes before cooking; this rest allows the potato to absorb the egg. The flip requires confidence: a plate must cover the pan completely, the pan inverted in one decisive motion.

items.preparation: peeled and thinly sliced, about 3 mm
for confiting the potato; most is drained off afterwards

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a 24 to 26 cm non-stick pan over the lowest heat. Add the potato slices, onion, and 1 teaspoon of salt. Cook very gently, turning occasionally, for 20 to 25 minutes until the potato is completely soft and the onion is completely sweet and translucent. The oil should bubble very gently; it should not fry. Drain in a colander, reserving 3 tablespoons of the oil.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl with the remaining 0.5 teaspoon of salt and pepper. Add the potato and onion mixture and mix gently. Leave to rest for 10 minutes.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the reserved oil in the pan over medium heat. Pour in the egg and potato mixture and spread evenly. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally, until the edges are set but the centre is still slightly soft. Place a large flat plate over the pan and, holding both firmly, invert in one smooth motion. Slide the tortilla back into the pan and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more. Slide onto a board and rest for 5 minutes before serving. Serve warm or at room temperature.
